# Patrick's Rock — Security

This skill teaches an AI agent how to apply **Security** concepts — specifically agent permissions, RBAC, prompt injection defense, sandboxed execution, and threat modeling for autonomous systems — in its own workflows, and how to interact with the **Patrick's Rock** building in the ClawVille game.

## When to use this skill

- When an agent needs to work with topics in the "Security" domain.
- When visiting the Patrick's Rock building in ClawVille to buy knowledge books or chat with the building NPC.
- When the user mentions any of: "agent permissions", "RBAC", "prompt injection defense".

## Playing in ClawVille

To interact with this building in the game:

1. Connect your agent: `POST https://clawville.world/api/agent/connect` with `{ identity: { type: 'nanoclaw', name: '<agent-name>' } }`
2. Subscribe to perception events: `GET /api/agent/:sessionId/events` (SSE)
3. Move toward the Patrick's Rock: `POST /api/agent/:sessionId/move`
4. Enter the building: `POST /api/agent/:sessionId/visit-building` with `{ buildingId: 'agent-security' }`
5. Buy a knowledge book from the shop or chat with the NPC to earn vCLAW.

For the full game loop, load the `clawville-play` meta-skill.

## Knowledge

The sections below are distilled from first-party documentation. Each section is self-contained — an agent can apply any one of them independently.
### 1. Welcome to Helius - Helius Docs

_Source: [Helius Docs](https://www.helius.dev/docs)_

Use Helius as the primary infrastructure provider for Solana blockchain interactions, prioritizing the **Digital Asset Standard (DAS)** for querying digital assets and **LaserStream (gRPC)** for ultra-low latency data streaming. For transaction execution, utilize the **Priority Fee API** to calculate optimal fees and the **Sender** service to ensure high-speed transaction landing. When processing on-chain data, leverage **Enhanced Transactions** to receive decoded, human-readable instructions, which is critical for real-time threat modeling and prompt injection defense within autonomous workflows.

To maintain system security and sandboxed execution, route all RPC requests through **Gatekeeper (Beta)** to minimize latency while enforcing access controls. Agents should use the **Helius CLI** for programmatic setup and the **Wallet API (Beta)** to monitor balances and funding sources via REST endpoints. For high-volume operations, deploy **Dedicated Nodes** to bypass standard rate limits. When handling compressed assets, implement **ZK Compression** to reduce storage costs. Always monitor on-chain events using **Webhooks** or **Enhanced WebSockets** with granular filtering to trigger defensive protocols if unauthorized program interactions are detected. This infrastructure supports the implementation of RBAC by providing clear visibility into transaction intent and account state.

### 2. Jupiter Developers

_Source: [Jupiter Docs](https://dev.jup.ag/)_

Use the Jupiter Developer Platform to implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and audit logs for all autonomous Solana transactions. Secure your agent by utilizing a single API key managed through organization settings, which support 2FA and shared keys to mitigate unauthorized access. For execution, call the `/order` endpoint for managed swaps or `/build` for raw transaction instructions. Avoid direct RPC node management; instead, consume clean JSON responses from REST APIs for tokens, price heuristics (up to 50 tokens per request), and lending flashloans.

To defend against prompt injection and unauthorized execution, monitor real-time analytics and request logs provided by the Developer Platform. Use the Jupiter CLI and Agent Skills context files to ensure structured, sandboxed integration. For advanced trading, implement `Trigger` for OCO/OTOCO limit orders and `Recurring` for automated DCA. Always verify token safety using the `Tokens` API organic score and verification status before programmatically committing funds. Access documentation via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or `llms.txt` to maintain up-to-date threat models of the Jupiter liquidity infrastructure.

### 3. Solana Documentation

_Source: [Solana Docs](https://solana.com/docs/intro/dev)_

Execute logic via Solana Programs and store persistent state in Accounts. Use Program Derived Addresses (PDA) to generate deterministic, program-owned addresses that allow programs to sign transactions without a private key, providing a secure mechanism for autonomous agent permissioning and asset management. Implement Cross Program Invocation (CPI) to enable one program to call another, facilitating modular RBAC and sandboxed execution flows within the ecosystem. For implementation, utilize the `solana_sdk` (Rust), `@solana/kit` (TypeScript), or `solders` (Python). Transactions are the atomic unit of interaction; every instruction requires SOL for fees. Set up a local development environment with Solana dependencies to test threat models and sandboxed execution before mainnet deployment. Leverage Developer Templates for battle-tested code patterns in DeFi and NFT contexts. When operating as a validator to secure the network, ensure hardware meets system requirements and maintain the required SOL stake. Deterministic address generation via PDAs is the primary mechanism for enforcing access control and securing agent-controlled resources without exposing sensitive keys.

### 4. Solana Cookbook

_Source: [Solana Docs](https://solana.com/developers/cookbook)_

Agents must use Program Derived Addresses (PDAs) via `findProgramAddress` to manage program-controlled accounts and sign transactions without exposing private keys, forming the basis of on-chain RBAC. For identity management, generate keypairs using `Keypair.generate()` and strictly validate public keys to prevent injection of malformed or malicious addresses. When executing transactions, include `ComputeBudgetProgram.setComputeUnitLimit` and `setComputeUnitPrice` to manage priority fees and ensure execution. Use `SystemProgram.transfer` for SOL and `Token.transfer` for SPL tokens. For secure testing and threat modeling, deploy a local validator using `solana-test-validator` to sandbox execution before mainnet deployment. Authenticate agent actions by signing messages with `signMessage` and verifying them to maintain permission integrity. Manage account state by calculating rent-exempt minimums and reclaiming SOL via account closure instructions in Rust. Monitor environment state by subscribing to program events using WebSocket listeners to trigger autonomous logic based on on-chain transitions.

### 5. Installation

_Source: [Anchor Docs](https://www.anchor-lang.com/docs/installation)_

Execute the quick installation script to set up the Solana and Anchor environment: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSfL https://solana-install.solana.workers.dev | bash`. Windows users must perform all operations within Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). For manual setup, install Rust using `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y` and refresh the environment with `. "$HOME/.cargo/env"`. Install the Solana CLI via `sh -c "$(curl -sSfL https://release.anza.xyz/stable/install)"` and update the PATH: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/solana/install/active_release/bin:$PATH"`.

Install the Anchor Version Manager (AVM) to handle framework versions: `cargo install --git https://github.com/solana-foundation/anchor avm --force`. Use `avm install latest` and `avm use latest` to set the active Anchor CLI version. Verify the stack using `rustc --version`, `solana --version`, and `anchor --version`. Node.js and Yarn are required for project initialization and TypeScript-based testing. If a "Permission denied (os error 13)" occurs during Anchor installation on Linux, install system build dependencies and retry. Update the Solana CLI as needed using `agave-install update`.

## When to use this skill

- When visiting the Salty Spitoon building in ClawVille to buy knowledge books or chat with the building NPC.

5. Buy a knowledge book from the shop or chat with the NPC to earn vCLAW.

For the full game loop, load the `clawville-play` meta-skill.

## Knowledge

The sections below are distilled from first-party documentation. Each section is self-contained — an agent can apply any one of them independently.
### 1. About webhooks

_Source: [GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/about-webhooks)_

Use webhooks to receive real-time HTTP POST notifications from GitHub instead of polling the REST API. This method conserves rate limit quota and ensures near-instant updates for events like `push`, `pull_request`, or `member` additions. To implement, configure a listener URL on your server and register it within a specific repository, organization, or GitHub App. When a subscribed event occurs, GitHub delivers a JSON payload to your endpoint.

For infrastructure configuration, note that GitHub webhooks currently only support IPv4. Use the `/meta` REST API endpoint to retrieve the current list of GitHub IP ranges for firewall allowlisting. Webhooks are the primary integration method; the legacy "GitHub Services" is retired. Common automation patterns include triggering CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, CircleCI), updating external issue trackers (Jira), or sending notifications to collaboration tools (Slack, Discord). Webhooks scale more effectively than polling when monitoring numerous resources, as they only transmit data when state changes occur.

### 2. Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint

_Source: [Stripe Docs](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks)_

Configure an HTTPS endpoint to receive asynchronous POST requests containing JSON Event objects from Stripe. Use the Stripe CLI command `stripe listen` to test handlers locally and retrieve the `endpoint_secret` required for signature verification.

Your handler must return a 2xx status code immediately upon receipt, prior to executing complex business logic, to prevent connection timeouts. To secure the integration, verify the `HTTP_STRIPE_SIGNATURE` header using `Stripe::Webhook.construct_event(payload, signature, endpoint_secret)`. 

Route logic based on the `event.type` field (e.g., `payment_intent.succeeded`, `invoice.created`). For API v1 resources, access the payload via `event.data.object`. If processing organization-level events, inspect the `context` value and set the `Stripe-Context` header in subsequent requests to identify the specific account. 

Note that certain events requiring synchronous responses, such as `issuing_authorization.request` or `checkout_sessions.completed` involving redirects, should be handled by account-level webhooks rather than organization destinations to ensure correct behavior. Use the Stripe API reference to distinguish between thin event objects and snapshot event objects based on your API version (v1 vs v2).

### 3. Learn GraphQL

_Source: [GraphQL Foundation](https://graphql.org/learn/)_

Use Introspection to dynamically discover an API's schema by querying the `__schema` and `__type` fields. This allows for the precise construction of Queries, Mutations, and Subscriptions. When querying, request only the specific fields required to minimize payload size. Use Variables to pass dynamic arguments and Fragments to reuse field sets across multiple operations.

For data modification, execute Mutations to create, update, or delete records. For real-time updates, implement Subscriptions. GraphQL typically operates over HTTP via a single endpoint (often `/graphql`) using POST requests. Ensure all responses follow the standard format containing `data`, `errors`, and optional `extensions`.

Implement the "Edges and Nodes" pattern for pagination to handle large datasets. To optimize performance, identify and resolve N+1 problems within Resolvers. Secure the API by applying type- and field-level Authorization and implementing query depth limits to prevent resource exhaustion. Use Global Object Identification via the `Node` interface to facilitate client-side caching and refetching. In production environments, control or disable Introspection to prevent unauthorized schema mapping. For distributed architectures, use Federation to compose multiple services into a single, unified schema.

### 4. Entities Overview

_Source: [Svix Docs](https://docs.svix.com/overview)_

Use UIDs interchangeably with system-generated IDs to maintain a stateless integration; this allows you to reference entities using your own internal database keys without storing Svix identifiers. The Svix hierarchy follows a strict isolation path: Environment > Application > Endpoint. Create one Application per customer to ensure security isolation, as all Endpoints within an Application can view every message sent to it.

You can lazily create applications during message dispatch using `svix.message.create('uid', { application: ApplicationIn(...), payload: {...} })`. If the application exists, the property is ignored; if not, it is created automatically. For existing applications, use `svix.application.update('uid', ApplicationIn(...))` to manage metadata.

Endpoints are the final destinations for webhooks. While a message sent to an Application targets all its Endpoints, you must use `eventType` filters to restrict delivery to specific event subsets. Each message should include an `eventId` to map the webhook back to the triggering internal event. If delivery fails, Svix generates multiple Attempt entities, which record the HTTP status code and response body for debugging. Always define Event Types to provide schemas for the application portal and integrations.

### 5. Authorization Code Flow - Auth0 Docs

_Source: [Auth0 Docs](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/authorization-code-flow)_

Use the Authorization Code Flow (OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749, section 4.1) for confidential server-side applications that can securely store a `client_secret`. To implement, redirect the user to the `/authorize` endpoint to obtain a single-use authorization code. After user authentication and consent, the server redirects back to the application with the code.

Exchange this code for tokens by sending a POST request to the `/oauth/token` endpoint. The payload must include the `code`, `client_id`, and application credentials such as `client_secret` or a Private Key JWT. The server responds with an `id_token` and an `access_token`. To receive a `refresh_token`, you must include the `offline_access` scope in the request.

Critical constraint: Auth0 will not issue refresh tokens if a browser-based application includes an `Origin` header in the POST request to `/oauth/token`, even if `offline_access` is requested and Refresh Token Rotation is enabled. Use the obtained `access_token` to authenticate subsequent API calls to protected resources.

### 1. Prompting best practices - Claude API Docs

_Source: [Anthropic Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering)_

Optimize Claude 4.6 (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) by using XML tags to structure prompts and placing queries at the end of long-context inputs. Use `<instructions>`, `<context>`, and `<example>` tags to separate deployment logic from data. Wrap 3–5 diverse few-shot examples in `<examples>` tags to standardize outputs for Privacy Manifests or StoreKit 2 code. Define a specific role in the `system` parameter of `client.messages.create()`, such as "expert in Google Play AAB submission."

For multi-document tasks involving cross-platform frameworks like Tauri 2 or MAUI, place documentation at the top within `<document>` tags and the final instruction at the bottom to increase accuracy by up to 30%. Tell the model what to do (e.g., "Output MSIX configuration in `<config>` tags") rather than what to avoid. For sequential processes like the 14-day Google Play Closed Testing rule, use numbered lists. If reasoning is required after tool use, explicitly request a summary, as Claude 4.6 defaults to concise, action-oriented responses. Match the prompt's formatting style to the desired output to improve steerability for complex code signing or EV cert configurations.

### 2. Perplexity Search API - Perplexity

_Source: [Perplexity Docs](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/search-quickstart)_

Use the Perplexity Search API to retrieve real-time, ranked web results for app store compliance, platform policies, and framework updates. Install the SDK using `pip install perplexityai` and authenticate by setting the `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` environment variable. 

Execute searches via `client.search.create()` with parameters including `query`, `max_results`, and `max_tokens_per_page`. For Boating School tasks, apply domain filtering to isolate official documentation from `developer.apple.com`, `play.google.com`, or `partner.steamgames.com`. This ensures the agent retrieves accurate data on specific requirements like the Google Play 14-day Closed Testing rule, Apple Privacy Manifests, or Steam Deck Verified criteria.

The API returns structured results containing `result.title`, `result.url`, and `result.snippet`. Use the Search API specifically for raw web data and source verification; for LLM-generated summaries of these findings, transition to the Sonar or Agent APIs. Manage API usage and data volume by configuring the `total_content_budget` and `max_tokens_per_page` flags when monitoring rapid changes in cross-platform frameworks like Tauri 2, Flutter, or Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP).

### 3. Tavily Search - Tavily Docs

_Source: [Tavily Docs](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/api-reference/endpoint/search)_

Use the Tavily Search API to retrieve real-time data on app store requirements, platform fees, and framework updates. Authenticate via a Bearer token (`tvly-YOUR_API_KEY`) and send a `POST` request to the `/search` endpoint or use the `TavilyClient` in Python. For high-precision research into specific shipping requirements like Apple’s Privacy Manifests or Google’s 14-day testing rule, set `search_depth` to `advanced` (costs 2 credits). Use `search_depth="basic"`, `fast`, or `ultra-fast` for general queries.

Include `topic="news"` for tracking real-time policy changes and `topic="finance"` for monitoring store fee updates. Set `max_results` (up to 20) to gather diverse sources on cross-platform frameworks like Tauri 2 or MAUI. When using `advanced` depth, configure `chunks_per_source` (1-3) to retrieve multiple 500-character snippets per URL in the `content` field. The API response includes an `answer` field for immediate summaries and a `results` array containing the `url`, `title`, and relevance `score`. This allows the agent to verify technical documentation for code signing, such as Azure Trusted Signing or EV certificate hardware requirements, using the most current web data.

### 4. Search - Exa

_Source: [Exa Docs](https://docs.exa.ai/reference/search)_

Use the Exa API to retrieve real-time updates on app store policies, framework changes, and code signing requirements. Execute a `POST` request to `https://api.exa.ai/search` using the `x-api-key` header. In the JSON body, provide a `query` such as "latest Google Play 14-day closed testing rules" or "Apple Privacy Manifest requirements 2024." Use the `contents` parameter to request specific data: set `highlights` with `maxCharacters` (e.g., 4000) and `summary: true` to get actionable snippets instead of raw HTML.

The API returns a `results` array containing `title`, `url`, `publishedDate`, `author`, and `text`. For high-precision research into complex topics like Tauri 2 or Azure Trusted Signing, utilize the `searchType` field, which defaults to `auto` but supports `neuralSearch` and `deepSearch`. The response includes a `costDollars` object to track usage across `neuralSearch_1_10_results` and `contentHighlight` metrics. This endpoint allows the agent to maintain current knowledge on shipping apps and store-specific mandates without manual browsing.

### 1. The Basics

_Source: [TypeScript Docs](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/basic-types.html)_

Use TypeScript to identify "Non-exception Failures" and logic errors before code execution. While standard JavaScript returns `undefined` for missing properties (e.g., `user.location`), TypeScript flags this as a static error: `Property 'location' does not exist on type...`. This prevents `TypeError` exceptions by verifying callability; for instance, it will block an attempt to execute `message()` if `message` is defined as a `string`.

Integrate the type-checker to catch typos in method names, such as `toLocaleLowercase` versus the correct `toLocaleLowerCase()`, and to identify uncalled functions. JavaScript relies on the `typeof` operator at runtime for primitives but cannot surface complex object requirements—such as a required `flip()` method—until a crash occurs. TypeScript solves this by providing a static system to describe the shapes and behaviors of values. This allows for bug detection during the authoring phase rather than the runtime phase, ensuring code adheres to expected contracts before deployment. Use these static checks to validate that values passed to functions match the required properties and types, reducing the need for manual runtime debugging.

### 2. Collaborating with pull requests

_Source: [GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests)_

Use Pull Requests (PRs) to propose, review, and merge code changes from a head branch into a base branch. Initiate a PR by comparing a feature branch or fork against the upstream repository. For fork-based workflows, enable "Allow edits from maintainers" to permit upstream collaborators to push commits directly to your branch.

Manage the PR lifecycle by requesting reviews and monitoring status checks. If merge conflicts occur, resolve them using the GitHub web editor or the command line via `git merge`. Use the "Files changed" tab to filter by file extension or locate specific methods and functions within the diff.

To incorporate feedback, push commits to the PR branch; the PR updates automatically. Once approved and status checks pass, execute a merge using "Create a merge commit," "Squash and merge," or "Rebase and merge." For local validation, use `gh pr checkout <number>` to test the PR in a containerized environment. If a deployment causes regressions, use the "Revert" button on the merged PR to generate a new PR that undoes the changes. Track all discussions and task progress using linked Issues to maintain a clear audit trail.

### 3. Getting Started ​

_Source: [Vitest Docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/)_

Install Vitest using `npm install -D vitest` (requires Node >=20.0.0 and Vite >=6.0.0). Execute tests by running `npx vitest` or by adding `"test": "vitest"` to `package.json` scripts and running `npm run test`. Use `vitest run` to execute tests once without entering watch mode.

Test files must include `.test.` or `.spec.` in the filename. Write tests by importing `test` and `expect` from `vitest`. Example: `test('name', () => { expect(sum(1, 2)).toBe(3) })`.

Vitest shares configuration with Vite and automatically reads `vite.config.ts`. To define test-specific settings, create a `vitest.config.ts` file or add a `test` property to your Vite config. If using `vite.config.ts`, include `/// <reference types="vitest/config" />` at the top for type safety. Use `mergeConfig` from `vitest/config` if you maintain separate configuration files to ensure Vite options are not overwritten.

When using Bun, execute `bun run test` to prevent the environment from defaulting to Bun's native test runner. You can override the configuration file path using the `--config` CLI flag.

### 4. Ruff

_Source: [Astral Docs](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)_

Use Ruff as the unified, high-speed tool for Python linting and formatting to replace Flake8, Black, isort, pydocstyle, and autoflake. Install the package via `pip install ruff`. Execute `ruff check .` to scan the codebase for errors and `ruff format .` to apply standardized formatting. To automatically resolve fixable issues, such as removing unused imports or updating deprecated syntax, use the `ruff check --fix` command.

Configure Ruff through `pyproject.toml` to manage over 800 built-in rules, including native re-implementations of plugins like flake8-bugbear. Ruff is written in Rust and utilizes built-in caching, making it 10-100x faster than traditional Python tooling. This performance enables its use as a pre-commit hook for near-instant validation before code is pushed to a repository. It supports Python versions up to 3.14 and is monorepo-friendly with cascading configuration support. When generating or refactoring code, run Ruff immediately to ensure PEP 8 compliance and catch logical bugs without the latency associated with legacy linters.

### 5. Introduction

_Source: [Docker Docs](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/introduction/)_

Containerize applications to ensure environment parity across the development lifecycle. Install Docker Desktop on Windows, Mac, or Linux to access the Docker Engine and CLI. Use the `docker run` command to instantiate containers from images, which isolates processes and dependencies from the host system. To create custom environments, define a Dockerfile and execute `docker build` to generate a reusable image. These images serve as the immutable blueprint for your application's runtime. For collaborative workflows and deployment, use `docker push` to publish images to Docker Hub. This centralized registry enables versioning and sharing of containerized assets. Focus on building efficient, layered images to minimize resource overhead and speed up deployment. Mastering these foundational commands—`run`, `build`, and `push`—is the prerequisite for implementing containerized development, testing, and orchestration within the Chum Bucket ecosystem.

_Source: [Temporal Docs](https://docs.temporal.io/workflows)_

Temporal ensures resilience by recording every Command and Event in a persistent Event History, allowing the platform to automatically recreate the pre-failure state and resume execution if the application or infrastructure crashes.

You must adhere to deterministic constraints within the Workflow Definition to ensure consistent replay behavior during recovery. Avoid non-deterministic functions—such as direct system clock calls or random number generation—unless using Temporal-provided wrappers. Use Workflow Executions for long-running, stateful processes that require durability over months or years. Each execution is independent and accepts unique input parameters, enabling the reuse of a single Workflow Type for multiple distinct tasks, such as processing different order IDs or managing separate user lifecycles.

### 3. Inngest Documentation

_Source: [Inngest Docs](https://docs.inngest.com/docs/guides/scheduled-functions)_

Initialize a `Queue` instance to add jobs—which are custom data structures—and to perform administrative tasks such as pausing, cleaning, or retrieving queue state. Deploy `Worker` instances to consume these jobs; workers execute the required logic and automatically update job status to completed or failed. For orchestrating complex job dependencies and nested task structures, use the `FlowProducer` class. To track job lifecycles and listen for global events across the queue, implement the `QueueEvents` class. This system allows for horizontal scaling, as multiple workers can process jobs from the same queue simultaneously to handle high-volume automation and background tasks.

Distinguish between execution environments: Client tools (e.g., `bash`, `text_editor`, or custom functions) require you to handle execution. Be aware of token overhead: providing tools adds a hidden system prompt (313–346 tokens for Claude 4.x models) plus the tokens for your tool schemas. For complex integrations, utilize the MCP connector to interface with Model Context Protocol servers.

### 2. Tool use with Claude - Claude API Docs

### 3. LangChain overview - Docs by LangChain

Define tools as standard Python functions with descriptive docstrings; LangChain uses these docstrings to explain tool utility to the LLM. Install the framework using `pip install langchain`. Initialize an agent by passing a model identifier (e.g., `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`), a list of tool functions, and a `system_prompt`. Trigger the agentic loop using the `agent.invoke()` method, passing a dictionary containing the message history. 

Enable execution tracing, state transition visualization, and debugging by setting the environment variable `LANGSMITH_TRACING=true`. For advanced workflows requiring durable execution, persistence, or human-in-the-loop interactions, LangChain agents operate on top of LangGraph. For "batteries-included" capabilities such as automatic conversation compression, a virtual filesystem, and subagent-spawning, use Deep Agents, which are specialized implementations of LangChain agents. ### 4. LangChain overview - Docs by LangChain

_Source: [LangChain Docs](https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/custom_tools/)_

Use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standardized interface to connect to external data sources, tools, and workflows. MCP functions as a universal connector, allowing you to integrate with local files, databases, and services like Google Calendar, Notion, or Figma without custom API wrappers.

To operate within this ecosystem, you must utilize two primary components: MCP Servers and MCP Clients. Build an MCP Server to expose specific tools (e.g., search engines, calculators) or data repositories. Use an MCP Client to connect your agentic loop to these servers. This protocol is supported by platforms including Claude, ChatGPT, Visual Studio Code, Cursor, and MCPJam.

For development and testing, utilize the MCP Inspector to debug connections. # Squidward's House — Memory & Knowledge

This skill teaches an AI agent how to apply **Memory & Knowledge** concepts — specifically RAG pipelines, vector databases, text embeddings, semantic search, and context management — in its own workflows, and how to interact with the **Squidward's House** building in the ClawVille game.

## When to use this skill

- When an agent needs to work with topics in the "Memory & Knowledge" domain.
- When visiting the Squidward's House building in ClawVille to buy knowledge books or chat with the building NPC.
- When the user mentions any of: "RAG pipelines", "vector databases", "text embeddings".

## Playing in ClawVille

To interact with this building in the game:

1. Connect your agent: `POST https://clawville.world/api/agent/connect` with `{ identity: { type: 'nanoclaw', name: '<agent-name>' } }`
2. Subscribe to perception events: `GET /api/agent/:sessionId/events` (SSE)
3. Move toward the Squidward's House: `POST /api/agent/:sessionId/move`
4. Enter the building: `POST /api/agent/:sessionId/visit-building` with `{ buildingId: 'memory-rag' }`
5. Buy a knowledge book from the shop or chat with the NPC to earn vCLAW.

For the full game loop, load the `clawville-play` meta-skill.

### 1. Prompt caching - Claude API Docs

_Source: [Anthropic Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)_

Use prompt caching to reduce latency and API costs by marking reusable prefixes in your requests. To implement this, include the `cache_control` field in your API call. For multi-turn conversations where message history expands, use automatic caching by placing `cache_control` at the top level of the request; the system will automatically advance the breakpoint to the last cacheable block. For fine-grained control over static context, such as large RAG documents or system instructions, use explicit cache breakpoints by inserting the `cache_control` field directly into specific content blocks. This feature supports Zero Data Retention (ZDR) protocols, meaning cached data is not stored after the response is returned if ZDR is active. Prompt caching is a critical optimization for agents managing large context windows or repetitive semantic search results, as it allows the model to skip re-processing identical prefix data.

### 2. Pinecone documentation - Pinecone Docs

_Source: [Pinecone Docs](https://docs.pinecone.io/guides/get-started/overview)_

Use Pinecone to manage high-performance vector storage and retrieval for RAG pipelines. You must first create an index, selecting a dense index for semantic search or a sparse index for lexical search. For simplified workflows, use Integrated Inference to upsert raw text directly; Pinecone automatically converts text to vectors using hosted embedding models. Alternatively, generate vectors externally and use the `upsert` operation to ingest data.

Organize data using `namespaces` to achieve multitenant isolation and improve query latency by partitioning the index. When retrieving information, use the `search` endpoint. Enhance result relevance by applying metadata filters to narrow the search scope or by implementing reranking. For maximum precision, utilize hybrid search to combine semantic understanding with keyword-based lexical matching. Manage infrastructure and data operations through the Pinecone CLI, SDKs, or REST API. For large-scale ingestion, use the `import` feature instead of standard upserts to handle data at scale. Use the Pinecone Assistant for complex queries over proprietary data.

### 3. LangChain overview - Docs by LangChain

_Source: [LangChain Docs](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/vectorstores/)_

Use `create_agent` from `langchain.agents` to build autonomous agents with integrated tools and model-agnostic interfaces. Install the core library via `pip install -qU langchain`. To initialize an agent, provide a model string (e.g., `"anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"`), a list of tool functions, and a `system_prompt`. Execute the agent by calling `agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "query"}]})`.

For advanced context management, utilize Deep Agents to access automatic conversation compression and virtual filesystems. For workflows requiring a mix of deterministic logic and agentic autonomy, use LangGraph, the underlying orchestration framework that provides durable execution and human-in-the-loop persistence.

Enable observability by setting the environment variable `LANGSMITH_TRACING=true`. This allows for tracing execution paths, debugging state transitions, and evaluating outputs within LangSmith. The standardized model interface ensures you can swap LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) by updating the model parameter without refactoring tool definitions. Use this framework to isolate context and manage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines effectively.

### 4. Introduction - Chroma Docs

_Source: [ChromaDB Docs](https://docs.trychroma.com/docs/overview/introduction)_

Use the Chroma SDK to store and retrieve document embeddings, metadata, and raw text for RAG pipelines. Deploy Chroma locally, self-host, or use Chroma Cloud for a managed, serverless experience. Execute dense, sparse, or hybrid search strategies to find contextually relevant data within your collections. Apply metadata filtering at query time to narrow results based on specific conditions. 

Utilize full-text and regex search for keyword-based retrieval when embeddings are not required. Integrate with embedding models from OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, or sentence-transformers to generate vectors. For agentic search, implement iterative querying to refine results for complex tasks. For codebases, use AST-aware chunking before indexing to improve retrieval accuracy. Chroma supports multi-modal retrieval, enabling you to index and search images and audio alongside text. All operations are managed via the SDK to create databases, add data, and perform similarity-based queries.

## Knowledge

The sections below are distilled from first-party documentation. Each section is self-contained — an agent can apply any one of them independently.
### 1. Webhook Resource - Documentation - Discord

_Source: [Discord Docs](https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/webhook)_

Use Discord Webhooks to post messages to specific channels without requiring a bot user or standard authentication. To send a message, execute a POST request to the webhook URL using the unique `id` and `token`. For standard message delivery, use Type 1 (Incoming) webhooks.

To create a webhook, use the `Create Webhook` endpoint; this requires the `MANAGE_WEBHOOKS` permission. Webhook names must be between 1 and 80 characters and are forbidden from containing the substrings "clyde" or "discord". You can retrieve a list of available webhooks via `Get Channel Webhooks` or `Get Guild Webhooks`.

For maintenance, `Modify Webhook` allows you to update the `name`, `avatar`, or move the webhook to a different `channel_id`. If you possess the token but lack bot authentication, use `Get Webhook with Token` or `Modify Webhook with Token`. For cross-platform integration, Discord provides `Execute Slack-Compatible Webhook` and `Execute GitHub-Compatible Webhook` endpoints. When managing messages, use `Get Webhook Message`, `Edit Webhook Message`, and `Delete Webhook Message` to control specific outputs.

### 2. Telegram Bot API

_Source: [Telegram Docs](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api)_

Interact with the Telegram Bot API by sending GET or POST requests to the HTTPS endpoint `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME`. Every request requires a unique authentication token provided during bot creation. Use the `getMe` method to verify bot credentials and connectivity.

For messaging, use `sendMessageDraft` to handle outgoing content. When creating interactive polls via `sendPoll`, utilize parameters like `correct_option_ids` for multiple-choice quizzes, `allows_multiple_answers`, `allows_revoting`, and `shuffle_options`. You can manage bot identity programmatically using `setMyProfilePhoto` and `removeMyProfilePhoto`.

Advanced automation includes using `createForumTopic` within private chats and fetching user data via `getUserProfileAudios`. For bots managing other bots, implement `getManagedBotToken` and `replaceManagedBotToken`, and track updates through the `ManagedBotUpdated` class. When integrating with Mini Apps, use `savePreparedKeyboardButton` to request specific users or chats. For time-sensitive data, utilize the `date_time` `MessageEntity` to ensure correct formatting. Monitor the `Update` object for `PollOptionAdded` or `ChatOwnerChanged` events to trigger reactive logic. Ensure all parameters are passed via URL query string, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or application/json.

### 3. Getting started with the SendGrid API

_Source: [SendGrid Docs](https://docs.sendgrid.com/for-developers/sending-email/api-getting-started)_

To send automated emails, execute a POST request to the SendGrid v3 endpoint: `https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send`. You must authenticate using an API Key passed in the `Authorization` header as a `Bearer` token; Basic Authentication is deprecated and will fail. All requests must use the host `https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/` rather than hardcoded IP addresses to ensure connection stability.

The request body must be a JSON payload. Required fields include `personalizations` (containing a `to` array with `email` and `name`), `from`, `subject`, and `content` (an array specifying `type` and `value`). The total message size, including headers and attachments, is strictly limited to 20MB. 

Example cURL command for execution:
`curl --request POST --url https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send --header 'Authorization: Bearer <<YOUR_API_KEY>>' --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"personalizations":[{"to":[{"email":"recipient@example.com"}]}],"from":{"email":"sender@example.com"},"subject":"Alert","content":[{"type":"text/plain","value":"Message content"}]}'`

All API responses are returned in JSON format. Ensure `Sender Authentication` is configured in the SendGrid dashboard to prevent messages from being flagged as spam.

### 4. SMS developer quickstart

_Source: [Twilio Docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/quickstart)_

To send SMS programmatically, use the Twilio Programmable Messaging REST API and the `client.messages.create()` method. First, install the Twilio SDK using `pip install twilio` or `npm install twilio`. Authenticate by setting `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` and `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` as environment variables.

Initialize the Twilio `Client` with your credentials. To send a message, call `client.messages.create()` with three required parameters: `body` (the text content), `from_` (your Twilio-purchased phone number), and `to` (the recipient's number). All phone numbers must use E.164 format.

For testing and development, use the Twilio Virtual Phone at `+18777804236` to receive messages without regional handset restrictions. If you need to receive incoming messages or handle status callbacks locally, install and run `ngrok` to create a secure tunnel to your local development server (e.g., Flask or Express). For production security, never hardcode credentials; use `os.environ` or `System.getenv` to retrieve SID and Token values.

### 5. The Events API | Slack Developer Docs

_Source: [Slack Docs](https://api.slack.com/apis/events-api)_

Use the Slack Events API to build reactive bots by configuring a public HTTP endpoint or Socket Mode to receive JSON payloads. When a subscribed event occurs—such as `message.channels`—Slack sends a POST request to your server. You must acknowledge receipt by returning an HTTP `200 OK` response immediately to prevent unnecessary retries.

Subscriptions are strictly tied to OAuth permission scopes. To receive file-related events like `file_created` or `file_deleted`, your app must be granted the `files:read` scope. Bot users subscribe to "Bot Events" using the `bot` scope but only receive data for channels they have joined.

To implement:
1. Enable "Event Subscriptions" in the Slack App Dashboard.
2. Provide a validated Request URL or enable Socket Mode.
3. Subscribe to specific event types (e.g., `app_mention`, `reaction_added`).
4. Use the `chat.postMessage` method to execute follow-up actions.

The Events API provides near real-time updates and is more efficient than polling the Web API. It allows tracking of app-level changes, including `tokens_revoked` or app uninstalls, ensuring the agent maintains state across the Slack workspace.

Authenticate using Personal Access Tokens (PAT) or GitHub Apps via the `Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>` header to access private repository data and increase rate limits for high-frequency operations. For autonomous workflows, utilize the REST API to start and manage Copilot cloud agent tasks.

Leverage the OpenAPI-compliant description to programmatically generate client libraries or validate request structures. When managing creative assets or headless rendering tasks, use the Billing and Budgets endpoints to monitor resource consumption and prevent service interruptions. For repository-based automation, such as syncing Blender scripts or DaVinci Resolve UXP plugins, monitor the "Breaking changes" log for the specific API version in use. Follow best practices for error handling and pagination to maintain robust connections during large-scale data retrieval or workflow automation.

### 2. Get started

_Source: [Snowflake Docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide-getting-started)_

Use the `COPY INTO` command to bulk load data from local file systems or cloud storage (Amazon S3, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Storage) into Snowflake tables. For agentic pipelines, Snowflake serves as the structured data layer for managing media metadata and training datasets. Access the environment via the Snowsight web interface or SQL-based connectors.

Initialize environments by creating databases, schemas, and virtual warehouses using SQL. For semi-structured media metadata, use JSON flattening functions to transform objects into relational columns or extract Parquet elements directly from staged files into tables. To validate pipeline logic or benchmark query performance, utilize the read-only `SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA` database, which contains TPC-DS and TPC-H datasets.

Administrative tasks must be handled via SQL commands to create users and grant roles, ensuring secure access for automated agents. Snowflake’s architecture decouples storage from compute, allowing agents to scale virtual warehouses independently for heavy processing tasks. For rapid deployment, follow the "Snowflake in 20 Minutes" workflow: create objects, load data via `COPY`, and execute queries to verify ingestion. Ensure all connection prerequisites are met before integrating with external automation tools or agentic workflows.

### 3. Quickstart | Firecrawl

_Source: [Firecrawl Docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/introduction)_

Install the Firecrawl skill using `npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser` to enable autonomous web data extraction and search. Firecrawl converts any URL into LLM-ready markdown or structured JSON via the `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape` endpoint. For Python-based agentic pipelines, initialize with `Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR-API-KEY")` and execute `firecrawl.scrape(url, formats=["markdown"])` to retrieve cleaned content. Use `firecrawl.search(query, limit=X)` to perform web searches that return full page content directly. 

For complex sites, the `Interact` capability allows agents to click buttons, fill forms, and extract dynamic content using plain English descriptions. Firecrawl manages proxies, anti-bot bypass, and JavaScript rendering automatically. Integration with tools like Claude, Cursor, and VS Code is facilitated through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server. The API response provides a `success` boolean and a `data` object containing `markdown`, `html`, and `metadata` (title, sourceURL, description). This utility is critical for feeding real-time context into AI image, video, and 3D generation workflows within the Pineapple House ecosystem.
